findings.title: canManage() grants group-management rights to admins that only have the `view` scope
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `true` when the caller has either `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` **or** `MANAGE` on the all-groups resource. `canManage()` (no argument) is the check behind `GroupPermissionEvaluator.requireManage()`, which `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` uses to authorize group creation. Consequently an admin granted only a read-only `view` permission on `Groups` can create top-level groups, a privilege escalation. The group-scoped variant `canManage(GroupModel)` correctly requires only `MANAGE`, confirming `VIEW` here is a copy/paste mistake. There is also no test asserting that a `view`-only permission is rejected for write operations (`testViewGroups` only exercises reads), so the bug is not caught.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses authorization Resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: Group resources in the FGAP v2 schema are stored with `name == group.getId()` (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`/`getOrCreateResource`), while `Resource.getId()` is a separate generated UUID. This method (a) calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, and `hasPermission` resolves the argument via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so the lookup always misses and the evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource — per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are therefore never detected here; and (b) adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, whereas callers (`UsersResource.searchForUser` via `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)`, and `UsersResource.getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`) expect group IDs and match them against group membership. Result: `GET /users/count` returns 0 (or wrong values) for an admin whose only visibility comes from group `view-members` permissions, inconsistent with `GET /users`, and the group-id filter pushed into the user query can never match. The V1 implementation correctly uses `resource.getName()`. Note also that `findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` returns the all-groups resource itself, whose name is `"Groups"` and is not a group ID, so it would be added to the set as a bogus group ID if an all-groups permission exists.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when the all-groups resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: In `hasPermission`, when no per-group resource is found the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, which returns `null` if the realm does not support the authorization schema (e.g. `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled() == false`) or if the `Groups` resource does not exist (realms whose admin-permissions client was created before this change). The returned value is used without a null check in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()`, producing an NPE / HTTP 500 on ordinary admin endpoints (group listing, user search) instead of a clean `false`. Note `MgmtPermissionsV2` is selected purely on the `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` feature flag, so a realm with the feature on but admin permissions turned off (while the admin-permissions client still exists) reaches this path.

findings.title: No cleanup of group authorization resources/permissions when a group is deleted under FGAP v2
findings.body: `AdminPermissions.registerListener` only registers the `GroupRemovedEvent` handler when the v1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature is enabled, and `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` anyway. With the new Groups resource type, deleting a group leaves the authorization `Resource` named with the group id plus every scope permission referencing it orphaned in the admin-permissions client forever. Beyond growing stale data, these orphan entries show up when listing permissions/resources in the admin API (where `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` cannot resolve them) and must be deleted manually. A removal hook (analogous to the v1 listener) should delete the group resource and its permissions.

findings.title: getResourceName() not extended for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` resolves friendly names only for `USERS` ("All users" / username). With `GROUPS` now a supported resource type, permissions created for a group resource fall through to `return resource.getDisplayName()`, which is `null` for resources created by `getOrCreateResource` (created with name only). As a result the admin API/console shows `null` instead of the group name (or "All groups") for group-scoped permissions, which is the exact problem the Users branch was added to solve.

findings.title: No migration path: existing admin-permissions clients never get the Groups resource and group scopes
findings.body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so realms that already enabled FGAP v2 before this change keep an admin-permissions client without the `Groups` resource and without the new `manage-membership`, `manage-members`, `view-members` scopes. In such realms creating a group permission fails in `getOrCreateResource` with `ModelException("No scopes found.")` (the scope lookup at line 125 returns null) and `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` gets a null all-groups resource. Either a migration that adds the missing resource/scopes or lazy creation is needed.

findings.title: switch on resourceType throws NullPointerException for a null resource type
findings.body: The new `switch (resourceType)` dereferences `resourceType`; a `null` value now produces an NPE (HTTP 500) whereas the previous `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` chain fell through to the explicit `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object ...")`. `getOrCreateResource` is reachable for policy representations other than `ScopePermissionRepresentation` (which is the only type validated by `throwExceptionIfResourceTypeOrScopesNotProvided`), so a request without `resourceType` can hit this. Guard for null and throw the validation error instead.

findings.title: Removal of the global canView() short-circuit causes per-group policy evaluation under FGAP v2
findings.body: `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` (and the same change in `GroupResource.getSubGroups`) no longer computes the realm-wide `canView()` once. With `GroupPermissionsV2`, each group in the page triggers `resourceStore.findByName`, `getResourceTypeResource`, `policyStore.findByResource` and a full policy evaluation — i.e. several DB round trips and an authz evaluation per group even for an admin holding a single all-groups `view` permission. For realms with many groups this is a measurable regression on group listing; the previous code evaluated the global permission once and skipped per-item evaluation.

findings.title: Feature check moved from event time to listener-registration time
findings.body: `registerListener` now evaluates `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` once, when the provider event listener is registered during factory initialization, instead of on each event. If the profile is not yet fully resolved at registration time (or registration happens before feature configuration), the listener is never registered and role/client/group permission cleanup on removal silently stops working for the whole server lifetime, with no error. Keeping the check inside `onEvent` (or asserting profile availability at registration) avoids this ordering dependency.

findings.title: Javadoc on requireManageMembers / getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is wrong
findings.body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but the implementation checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` — a copy/paste error that misleads implementors of the interface. Additionally `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is documented as returning a "Stream of IDs" while it returns a `Set<String>`.

findings.title: Removal of public static ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes breaks compiled extensions
findings.body: `public static Stream<GroupModel> searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...)` is deleted outright. Although it lives in `server-spi-private`, that module is compiled against by custom providers; any extension calling this helper will fail with `NoSuchMethodError` after upgrade. If removal is intended, deprecate-and-delegate (or at least note the removal in upgrade docs) rather than removing in the same release.
